{"command":"docs sdk","data":{"content":"# Parameters, results, and failure semantics

Read exact defaults in the linked [signature index](index.md). Methods with similar
names may have different defaults; do not transfer a CLI flag or Playwright parameter
into a UIAutoma SDK call.

## Query and ownership

- `selector` in `find/find_all` is a saved asset name or `package.selector(...)`,
  not CSS, XPath, an observation ref or a raw runtime UUID. It needs the current Package.
- `find` returns one live element and rejects missing or ambiguous matches.
  `find_all` returns a list; check its length and actual contents.
- Web `find_by_css/find_by_xpath` and their `find_all_*` variants operate directly on
  the current page/element and do not require a Package. These are UIAutoma elements,
  not official Playwright Locator objects.
- Window/page operations without saved selectors do not require a Package.
  Live objects retain the creating connection. Navigation, removal or connection
  closure can invalidate them; obtain a new object from the intended target.
- `web.get(title=..., url=...)` uses substring matching by default and chooses a
  newer matching tab when several match. It does not enforce uniqueness. For an
  exact page, enumerate with `web.get_all`, compare `get_url()` to the intended
  full URL and reject zero or multiple exact matches. A base URL also matches
  its hash routes. Use `connect_page(page_ref)` for the Playwright route.
- SDK `timeout`, `load_timeout`, `connect_timeout`, `delay_after` and `duration`
  are seconds. `send_key_delay` and `focus_timeout` are milliseconds.
  Do not assume every API supports an infinite timeout. Element wait APIs document
  `0` as one check and `-1` as indefinite; use bounded waits for unattended work.

## Element input and pointer parameters

| Parameter | Meaning / valid values |
| --- | --- |
| `button` | `left`, `right`, `middle` |
| `keys` | `none` or a modifier combination such as `ctrl+shift` |
| `simulative` | Select the product's simulated/native strategy; backend support varies. It is not a promise that the window stays in the background. |
| `text`, `value` | Text to enter/set; do not put secret values in diagnostic output. |
| `append` for input | False replaces existing contents; True appends. |
| `contains_hotkey` | Whether keyboard syntax inside text is interpreted as keys rather than literal text. |
| `click_before_input` | Click the input target first; this may activate its window. |
| `force_ime_ENG` / `force_ime_eng` | Win element and Web spellings differ; use the exact signature. |
| `move_speed` | `instant`, `fast`, `middle`, `slow` |
| `behavior` for dragging | `smooth`, `instant` |
| `anchor` | `top_left`, `top_center`, `top_right`, `middle_left`, `middle_center`, `middle_right`, `bottom_left`, `bottom_center`, `bottom_right`, `random`; None means center. Also accepts `(anchor, offset_x, offset_y)` or corresponding keys in a dict. |

`input`/`clipboard_input` return None. Clipboard input uses the system clipboard;
do not rely on it as a way to set persistent clipboard contents.
Web input's optional `input_check`, `retry_times`, and `check_value` concern its
built-in text verification, not permission for the Agent to replay unrelated actions.
`set_value` uses the automation/value path rather than a typed-key workflow.

For Win, default `input` clicks the target and types keys; `focus_timeout` is a
delay after focus preparation, not proof that focus remains on that control.
`set_value` replaces the value through the control's automation interface.
Clipboard input pastes via the system clipboard. Choose the method for the
application's behavior: assigning a value need not trigger the same keyboard
events as typing. Read back the value and verify the application's result;
do not automatically retry with a different method after an uncertain action.
`move_mouse=False` suppresses the visible travel, not the final positioning or
click. It does not make an operation background-only.

`check(mode=...)` accepts `check`, `uncheck`, `toggle`. Prefer desired-state check or
uncheck over toggle for a known task. `select(item, mode=...)` supports `fuzzy`,
`exact`, `regex`; SDK selection rules are not the CLI's exact-text-only contract.
Indexes are zero-based; supported element selection APIs accept -1 for the last option.
Read Web-specific multi-selection rules in [browser contracts](browser.md).

## Common results

| API family | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Element click/input/hover/check/select/drag/highlight | None on successful completion; inspect the UI for business success. Element `last_result` holds available action diagnostics. |
| `get_text`, `get_html` | String |
| `get_value`, `get_attribute` | String or None when no value/attribute is available |
| Win `get_all_attributes` | Dict of names to values; values need not all be strings |
| Web `get_all_attributes` | Dict of attribute names to string values |
| `get_all_select_items`, `get_selected_item` | List of strings, not a single selected string |
| `get_select_options` (Web) | List of dicts with `name`, `value`, `selected` |
| Element `screenshot(folder_path, file_name=...)` | Saved PNG path string |
| WebBrowser `screenshot(...)` | None, unlike element screenshot |
| `exists`, state checks, element appearance/disappearance waits | Boolean; not all window waits return bool (see signature). |
| Web related-node lookup | `parent/child_at/previous_sibling/next_sibling` can return None; `children` returns a list |
| Win related-node lookup | Element or list; do not assume the Web nullable contract |

`ActionResult` diagnostics include `error`, `trace_info`, `strategy`,
`fallback_reason`, `clicked_point`, `log_lines`, and `trace_id`; absence of diagnostics
is not proof of success. Ordinary scripts should use exceptions and observable results,
not parse internal raw payloads.

## Windows, coordinates and screenshots

`window.get_detail()` returns a detail dict. With `operation`, it returns the value
for `title`, `text`, `process_name`, `class_name`, `handle`/`hwnd`, or `rect`; an unknown
key returns an empty string. Obtain a window with `win32.get_by_handle(actual_hwnd)`
when the precise handle is known. `window.close()` requests closure, which may prompt.

`set_state` accepts normal/show/restore, max/maximize/maximized,
min/minimize/minimized, hide. Use only the state the task needs.
`get_screen_size/get_real_resolution` return `(width, height)`;
`GetDeviceScaleFactor(125)` returns 1.25. Main-screen size is not a virtual-desktop rectangle.

Win element `get_bounding` returns `(x, y, width, height)`; Web returns a dict with
those keys. `to96dpi=True` is normalized geometry; `False` requests physical pixels.
Web `relative_to` is `screen` or `window` (client area); Win supports `screen`,
`window` (top-level window) and `client`. Do not mix normalized coordinates
with native physical mouse input. Negative screen coordinates are valid on multiple monitors.
Win drag `left/top` are relative physical-pixel offsets from the chosen starting anchor.

`win32.screenshot.save_*_to_file` returns a path, clipboard variants return None;
manual screenshot functions involve user region selection. `image_format` can be
inferred from the output path. Rectangle inputs use left/top/right/bottom, not width/height.
`clipboard.set_files` takes existing absolute paths; `get_file_paths` returns a list.
Clipboard reads/writes and global `send_keys/mouse_*` affect the current desktop target;
prefer element-scoped actions when possible.

## Errors and known limits
